question: What primary factor drives many Nigerian adolescents toward clandestine pregnancy terminations?

options.A: Encouragement from local peer pressure groups
options.B: Abundant availability of safe surgical clinics
options.C: A preference for traditional herbal remedies
options.D: Fear of social stigma and severe judgment

explanation: Adolescents often hide pregnancies and avoid formal hospitals because they fear being judged, scolded, or exposed by healthcare workers or their communities. [learn more](BMP320_U3_T3#BMP320_U3_T3_h1)

question: Which of the following best describes an unsafe abortion?

options.A: A legal procedure performed inside a tertiary teaching hospital
options.B: Any pregnancy loss occurring naturally before twenty weeks
options.C: Taking emergency contraceptive pills within seventy-two hours
options.D: A termination done without proper skills or safe medical standards

explanation: An abortion is classified as unsafe when it is performed by unqualified individuals or in places that fail to meet basic clinical safety standards. [learn more](BMP320_U3_T3#BMP320_U3_T3_h1)

question: What financial barrier frequently prevents young girls from accessing safe medical care?

options.A: Lack of personal income to pay for services
options.B: Expensive transport fares to foreign countries
options.C: High cost of government health insurance cards
options.D: Mandatory taxes placed on reproductive clinics

explanation: Because most adolescents are financially dependent, they cannot afford the fees charged by safe, regulated medical facilities. [learn more](BMP320_U3_T3#BMP320_U3_T3_h2)

question: Why do restrictive legal frameworks contribute to high rates of unsafe procedures?

options.A: They successfully eliminate all unwanted pregnancies across the nation
options.B: They force doctors to provide free surgical care in public hospitals
options.C: They make modern contraceptives completely illegal for adults
options.D: They force the entire process underground, creating secrecy and fear

explanation: Strict laws do not stop abortions from happening; instead, they drive desperate teenagers to seek dangerous, clandestine alternatives. [learn more](BMP320_U3_T3#BMP320_U3_T3_h2)

question: Which crude item is sometimes used by unqualified persons attempting mechanical termination?
explanation: Unqualified practitioners often resort to sharp, unsterilized household objects like knitting needles or bicycle spokes to rupture the membranes. [learn more](BMP320_U3_T3#BMP320_U3_T3_h3)

question: What major physiological damage occurs when caustic substances like bleach are inserted vaginally?

options.A: Permanent immunity against future pelvic inflammatory disease
options.B: Immediate relaxation of the circular cervical muscles
options.C: Rapid and painless expulsion of the products of conception
options.D: Severe chemical burns and localized tissue necrosis

explanation: Caustic household chemicals destroy delicate vaginal and uterine tissues on contact, leading to severe burns, bleeding, and tissue death. [learn more](BMP320_U3_T3#BMP320_U3_T3_h3)

question: What physical sign indicates that a uterine perforation with peritonitis has likely occurred?

options.A: Painless swelling of the lower extremities
options.C: Complete absence of any vaginal discharge
options.D: Elevated blood pressure and flushed skin

explanation: Peritonitis causes the abdominal wall muscles to become tight and rigid, accompanied by severe tenderness when touched. [learn more](BMP320_U3_T3#BMP320_U3_T3_h4)

question: A young female adolescent is rushed to the emergency ward pale, sweating, with a rapid pulse and heavy bleeding after a secret procedure. What is the immediate priority?

options.A: Interview family members about who performed the act
options.B: Resuscitate for hypovolemic shock and stabilize vitals
options.C: Delay treatment until police permission is documented
options.D: Administer oral iron tablets and discharge home

explanation: Saving the patient's life takes precedence in an emergency, requiring immediate stabilization of blood volume and vital signs. [learn more](BMP320_U3_T3#BMP320_U3_T3_h4)

question: What condition involving intrauterine scar tissue can result from aggressive uterine curettage?
explanation: Scraping the uterine cavity too aggressively destroys the lining, causing walls to stick together, which is known as Asherman's syndrome. [learn more](BMP320_U3_T3#BMP320_U3_T3_h5)

question: How does chronic pelvic infection following a bad abortion often cause infertility?

options.A: By altering the hormonal output of the thyroid gland
options.B: By completely stopping the monthly menstrual cycle
options.C: By scarring and blocking the fallopian tubes
options.D: By destroying all immature eggs stored in the ovaries

explanation: Infections cause inflammation that leaves scar tissue behind, blocking the passage where egg and sperm normally meet. [learn more](BMP320_U3_T3#BMP320_U3_T3_h5)

question: What standard clinical tool is frequently used for safe uterine evacuation during post-abortion care?
explanation: MVA is the safe, recommended standard method for clearing retained products of conception from the uterus. [learn more](BMP320_U3_T3#BMP320_U3_T3_h6)

question: Why is contraceptive counseling an essential component of emergency post-abortion care?

options.A: It punishes the patient so she avoids getting pregnant again
options.B: Fertility returns very quickly, risking rapid repeat unwanted pregnancy
options.C: It permanently prevents the development of future infections
options.D: Hospitals are legally required to sell family planning drugs

explanation: Ovulation can resume within weeks following an abortion, making immediate contraceptive counseling vital to prevent another crisis. [learn more](BMP320_U3_T3#BMP320_U3_T3_h6)

question: What is the primary characteristic of youth-friendly health services?

options.A: Strict requirement for parental consent before entry
options.B: Confidentiality and welcoming attitudes without judgment
options.C: Provision of care exclusively through religious organizations
options.D: Mandatory reporting of all teen patients to school principals

explanation: Youth-friendly centers succeed by guaranteeing privacy and treating young clients with respect rather than condemnation. [learn more](BMP320_U3_T3#BMP320_U3_T3_h7)

question: Which of the following is NOT an effective strategy for preventing unsafe adolescent abortions?

options.B: Withholding contraceptive information to discourage premarital sex
options.C: Dispelling common myths about modern birth control methods
options.D: Providing comprehensive sexuality education in local schools

explanation: Hiding contraceptive information does not stop sexual activity; it only increases the incidence of unprotected sex and unwanted pregnancies. [learn more](BMP320_U3_T3#BMP320_U3_T3_h7)
